name: Recent funding rounds
blurb: read where capital just flowed to infer where a market is heating up, then find the underserved adjacency.

name: Three-star reviews
blurb: mine lukewarm reviews of existing products; the specific, repeated complaints are a product spec someone hasn't built yet.

name: Investigate the graveyard
blurb: study startups that died with a good core idea; failure was often timing or execution, not the concept — and timing may have flipped.

name: Investigate science fiction
blurb: treat sci-fi as an accidental product roadmap; make the imagined solution real once the tech exists.

name: Acqui-deaths
blurb: hunt the gaps left when a big company acquires a startup and lets the original product wither; its orphaned users are your beachhead.

name: What won't change
blurb: build on the human constants (cheaper, faster, more convenient); durable value anchored to desires that never move.

name: Dominate fragmented categories
blurb: find a market with no clear leader and consolidate it under one brand and one standard.

name: Unbundling
blurb: split a bundled product into standalone pieces and win a segment the bundle over-serves or over-charges.

name: Niche down
blurb: pick a hyper-specific segment and become its specialist; depth beats breadth for a new entrant.

name: Rebrand boring products
blurb: take an essential-but-dull product, add design and story, and capture a big market (glasses, mattresses).

name: Premium boring products
blurb: add quality, design, and branding to a commodity to turn it into a near-luxury (vacuum cleaners, razors).

name: Democratize luxury
blurb: take a high-end product down-market over time, starting premium and driving toward mass affordability (EVs).

name: One-time-payment software
blurb: win the users who hate subscriptions by offering a comparable tool for a single fee.

name: Rebrand old supplements / categories
blurb: refresh a tired, trusted category with modern brand, format, and channel.

name: Build the anti-product
blurb: deliberately do the opposite of the category leader for the customers alienated by the norm.

name: Build a copycat
blurb: replicate a proven model and execute better or adapt it to a new context (social networks, super-apps).

name: Business-model arbitrage
blurb: port a proven business model from one industry to another that hasn't adopted it yet.

name: Industry timing arbitrage
blurb: take newly matured technology from one industry and apply it to another that hasn't adopted it.

name: Leverage patent expiry
blurb: when protection lapses, build the improved or cheaper version of a formerly-protected product.

name: Localize a global model
blurb: adapt a working overseas model to local conditions, regulation, and taste.

name: Disruptive innovation
blurb: enter a big, over-served market with something initially worse but cheaper/more accessible; improve until you overtake incumbents (the YC favorite).

name: Find shareable resources
blurb: spot underused assets that could be shared efficiently (spare rooms, idle cars).

name: Build gadget accessories
blurb: when a new hardware platform takes off, be ready with the complementary products for the gold rush.

name: Build on platforms
blurb: build atop an emerging platform's distribution before the platform (or others) fill the gap — with eyes open to platform risk.

name: Invent a new sport / category
blurb: combine familiar elements into something new that taps competitiveness and is easy to learn, hard to master.

name: Vertical AI agents
blurb: take one industry's high-value workflow end-to-end with a model wrapped in domain data, tools, guardrails, and system-of-record ownership. → deep profile in `02-frameworks-sample.md`.

name: Wrap-a-model → own-the-workflow
blurb: start as a thin layer on a base model, then race to own the data and workflow before the base model commoditizes the feature.

name: AI-native rebuild of a legacy workflow
blurb: re-architect a pre-AI SaaS category assuming the model does the core work (support, docs, reconciliation).

name: Data-moat-first
blurb: design the product to accumulate proprietary, non-substitutable data from day one; the app is the means, the data loop is the end.

name: Deprecation surfing
blurb: when an incumbent kills or degrades a feature (or a model provider deprecates a capability), catch the orphaned users.

name: Agent-arbitrage / orchestration
blurb: sit between customers and multiple AI agents/models, adding routing, evals, and guardrails as the value layer.

name: Regulatory-arbitrage in AI
blurb: build where compliance is the hard part (health, legal, finance) and make the guardrails the moat.
